newsitem.title: KENYA: Aid agencies threaten to suspend aid to Mogadishu.
newsitem.headline: Aid agencies threaten to suspend aid to Mogadishu.

text.p: Aid agencies and donors said on Monday they would suspend aid to Mogadishu on Wednesday unless an aid worker kidnapped and seriously wounded two weeks ago is released.

The Somali Aid Coordination Body (SACB) said Hilal Aden, a Somali human rights activist with the Life and Peace Institute agency, was being held without qualified medical treatment despite being kidnapped in north Mogadishu on September 19.

"Following the lack of a response from the competent Somali authorities...the SACB recommends that all international assistance to Mogadishu be suspended from 2 October unless Mr Aden has been released," it said in a statement.
The Nairobi-based SACB, which groups donors and aid agencies operating in Somalia, said it was "deeply concerned" about Aden, who was seriously wounded when he was kidnapped.
Kidnappings and extortion are common in Mogadishu where weapons are easily available and unemployment high since the departure of the U.N. peacekeeping operation in March 1995.
Somalia has had no central government and has been divided between rival clan-basked militias which frequently clash since the overthrow of late president Mohamed Siad Barre in 1991.
